node-1.label: A man in his 60s presented with a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid for 1 year

node-2.label: Physical examination revealed a 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on the right upper eyelid

node-3.label: The patient is a man in his 60s with no remarkable medical history

why.why: Pathologist and laboratory physician analyses both confirm that the CD4-predominant, monoclonal T-cell infiltrate with atypical lymphocytic exocytosis is diagnostic of a malignant cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides) involving the eyelid. This further supports malignant eyelid neoplasm; the missing staging workup affects staging, not the malignant nature of the lesion, so confidence is increased from 0.95 to 0.96.

The laboratory physician analysis independently concludes that benign inflammatory dermatosis is essentially excluded by the monoclonal T-cell rearrangement and CD4-predominant atypical infiltrate. No new evidence supports a reactive inflammatory process, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.04.

The laboratory physician analysis independently concludes that autoimmune skin disease is essentially excluded by the clonal T-cell infiltrate. The findings point to a malignant T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder rather than an autoimmune process, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.04.

node-13.label: Staging workup for mycosis fungoides has not been performed (no flow cytometry, peripheral blood Sézary cell examination, or staging imaging)

Histopathology showing atypical lymphocytic exocytosis, immunohistochemistry showing a CD4-predominant infiltrate with CD4:CD8 >7:1, and T-cell gene rearrangement detecting a monoclonal T-cell population collectively provide conclusive evidence for a specific malignant entity: mycosis fungoides involving the eyelid. Both pathologist and laboratory physician analyses independently confirm this diagnosis, making this the appropriate fine-grained refinement of the frontier.

node-17.label: Laboratory physician analysis states that extracutaneous involvement cannot be fully excluded because staging workup (flow cytometry, peripheral blood Sézary cell count, CT/PET) remains unavailable

node-18.label: No direct evidence of extracutaneous involvement or Sézary cells is currently available

node-19.label: Mycosis fungoides is currently confined to the skin (no extracutaneous involvement)

attrs.why: The pathologist currently considers the disease limited to the skin, and both experts note there is no direct evidence of extracutaneous lesions or Sézary cells. Although staging workup has not been completed, the available evidence favors skin-limited disease, so confidence is 0.75.

node-1.label: A man in his 60s presented with a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid for 1 year

node-2.label: Physical examination revealed a 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on the right upper eyelid

node-3.label: The patient is a man in his 60s with no remarkable medical history

why.why: Pathologist and laboratory physician analyses both confirm that the CD4-predominant, monoclonal T-cell infiltrate with atypical lymphocytic exocytosis is diagnostic of a malignant cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides) involving the eyelid. This further supports malignant eyelid neoplasm; the missing staging workup affects staging, not the malignant nature of the lesion, so confidence is increased from 0.95 to 0.96.

The laboratory physician analysis independently concludes that benign inflammatory dermatosis is essentially excluded by the monoclonal T-cell rearrangement and CD4-predominant atypical infiltrate. No new evidence supports a reactive inflammatory process, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.04.

The laboratory physician analysis independently concludes that autoimmune skin disease is essentially excluded by the clonal T-cell infiltrate. The findings point to a malignant T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder rather than an autoimmune process, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.04.

node-8.label: Immunohistochemistry shows CD4-predominant infiltrate with CD4:CD8 ratio >7:1

node-9.label: T-cell gene rearrangement study detects a monoclonal T-cell population

node-10.label: Pathologist diagnoses mycosis fungoides involving the eyelid, a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

node-11.label: Mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) involving the right upper eyelid

why.why: Both the pathologist and laboratory physician analyses independently confirm that the histopathologic findings—atypical lymphocytic exocytosis, CD4:CD8 >7:1, and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement—are diagnostic of mycosis fungoides involving the right upper eyelid. The laboratory physician also recommends staging workup, but the absence of staging does not reduce diagnostic confidence in the eyelid lesion, so confidence is increased from 0.92 to 0.95.

node-12.label: Laboratory physician analysis confirms mycosis fungoides involving the right upper eyelid and recommends completing staging workup

node-13.label: Staging workup for mycosis fungoides has not been performed (no flow cytometry, peripheral blood Sézary cell examination, or staging imaging)

node-14.label: Mycosis fungoides may have extracutaneous/systemic involvement

why.why: The pathologist and laboratory physician analyses both state that staging workup remains unavailable, so extracutaneous involvement cannot be fully excluded; however, neither provides any direct evidence of extracutaneous lesions or Sézary cells, and the pathologist currently considers the disease limited to the skin. The absence of direct evidence further lowers the probability of extracutaneous/systemic involvement from 0.3 to 0.2, pending completion of staging workup.
